decisions.quote: We retained our previous sample of 10 women with PMDD and 15 healthy comparison women (cohort 1) and added a second independent cohort of 24 women with PMDD and 61 healthy comparison women (cohort 2). All participants underwent the same ovarian steroid hormone manipulation paradigm. We evaluated differences between cohorts, attempted to replicate our original findings of a differential behavioral sensitivity to otherwise similar changes in ovarian steroids in women with PMDD compared to healthy comparison women (3), and examined several as yet unanswered questions about the effects of ovarian steroids on symptoms in these women.

decisions.quote: The study results confirm that leuprolide-induced suppression of ovarian hormones in women with PMDD can reduce symptom severity and eliminate PMDD symptom cyclicity. We further confirmed that several core symptoms recur in women with PMDD during ovarian steroid addback. We found that 69% of the women with PMDD met response criteria to induced ovarian suppression, which is consistent with the literature (3, 28–32). Moreover, negative affective symptoms recurred in the majority (but not all) of these leuprolide responders. This confirms and replicates our original finding that women with PMDD and healthy comparison women who do not have PMDD have different behavioral responses to the same physiological exposures to both estradiol and progesterone, a phenomenon that, in this experimental paradigm, distinguishes women with PMDD from women without.
decisions.reason: With the target identity resolved to Schmidt et al. (1998, ref. 3), the authors state an explicit overall verdict that their study confirms and replicates the original finding of differential behavioral responses to physiological estradiol and progesterone addback in women with PMDD compared with healthy comparison women, with no significant cohort differences between cohorts 1 and 2. Analyses of progesterone-specific irritability/mood-swing severity, physical symptoms, and hormone delta correlations are explicitly framed as new extension questions.
